Progress meeting · December 2025

Validating ORAC SLSTR cloud retrievals against EarthCARE

Sentinel-3A × EarthCARE — a polar simultaneous-nadir-overpass validation of cloud-top height, optical depth, effective radius, water path, cloud mask and phase.

The one story
Two independent limitations of the polar-daytime solar retrieval: a bright-surface optical-depth saturation and an intrinsic liquid phase bias. Thermal CTH is strong; CER is robust.
Sample
Antarctic-summer daytime (solar variables); bi-hemispheric for thermal CTH. 0.6 M matched pixels, December 2025.

References · A-CTH / ACM-CAP / A-EBD / A-TC

01 / Method

A polar comparison — by orbital mechanics, not choice

Collocation density — SLSTR × EarthCARE crossings, Dec 2025
  • Two sun-synchronous orbiters coincide only near the poles (~70–83°) — every match is polar, irreducibly.
  • Match rule: temporal gate ±60 min + nearest pixel < 3 km (SLSTR ≈ EarthCARE ≈ 1 km footprint).
  • Solar retrievals need daylight → December = Antarctic polar day → the COT/CER/CWP/phase sample is 100% Southern Hemisphere; thermal CTH also samples the Arctic (night).

02 / Cloud-top height

The strong result

ORAC CTH vs EarthCARE A-CTH
  • Median CTH bias −0.25 km (Antarctic, polar day) — the thermal cloud-top retrieval survives the polar regime.
  • Arctic (polar night) −0.95 km: ~4× larger — a night-vs-day + winter-sea-ice regime contrast, not a pole effect.
  • The only variable that samples both hemispheres; the headline −0.57 km blends the two regimes.

03 / Optical depth

The passive retrieval saturates

ORAC liquid τ vs ACM-CAP τ (radar-aided synergy)
  • Report the median: −4.8. The quoted "+3 mean" is a skew artefact of a high-τ tail — it even flips sign.
  • ORAC's passive liquid τ is pinned ~5–8 across the entire ACM-CAP range (0.6→34): over-reads thin cloud, saturates on thick, cannot correlate.
  • It is ORAC saturating, not the radar reference being high (CPR shifts the bias by ~1 τ).

04 / Surface control

The deficit is cryospheric — the surface, not the phase

Median bias & correlation by surface type
  • Water-COT correlates (r = +0.28) and over-reads only over open water; over sea-ice & ice-sheet (95% of the scene) r → 0 and bias is −4 to −5.
  • Same clouds, only the background changed → the τ saturation is the bright-surface radiative regime, not an algorithm bug.
  • CER is surface-robust (median +0.2 / +0.3 µm): trustworthy droplet size even where τ is unconstrained.

05 / Water path

The saturation reaches the water budget

ORAC cwp vs ACM-CAP integrated liquid-water-content (LWP)
  • ORAC liquid water path runs 34% low on the median (30 vs 47 g m⁻²), decorrelated, worse over ice sheet (−18) than ocean (−13).
  • Validated against a radar+lidar water-content reference that never sees τ — confirming the saturation propagates into the water budget.
  • Fixed by the same surface-albedo advance, not a CWP-specific change.

06 / Phase & cloud mask

Two-way validation against EarthCARE A-TC

Confusion matrix · cloud-mask contingency · phase skill by surface
  • Phase: POD_liquid 89.5%, POD_ice 62.4% → ORAC has a liquid bias, calling 38% of ice cloud tops "liquid".
  • Cloud mask: POD 0.69, FAR 0.11 — conservative; the missed 31% is 88% thin cirrus the lidar sees and a passive imager cannot.
  • The phase bias is surface-independent (62–64% everywhere) — intrinsic, distinct from the surface-driven τ saturation.

08 / Summary

What's validated, and what's next

Validated — median-primary, with CIs

  • CTH · water-COT · ice-COT · CER · CWP · cloud mask · phase
  • Plus collocation methodology, surface-type & phase stratification, and sensitivity to Δt / distance.

The unifying result

  • Bright-surface τ saturation — surface-driven, propagates into CWP, spares open water.
  • Intrinsic liquid phase bias — POD_ice 62%, surface-independent.
  • Thermal CTH strong; CER robust — the trustworthy products over the cryosphere.

Next steps — need new processing

  • Arctic / boreal-summer month — run COT/CER/CWP/phase over Arctic sea-ice & Greenland.
  • Sentinel-3B (SLSTR-B) — second platform, cross-check.
  • Other seasons — the seasonal cycle.

Data ceilings

  • Low/mid latitudes are impossible with this orbital pairing — polar by construction.
